messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE fired: quota-anomaly on limiter-service.prod (region-us). PD incident INC-2026 created. symptom=spike in 429s to /v1/generate and /v1/chat (15% global), start=2026-03-14T04:12:10Z, suspected component=quota-mapper or limiter-heartbeat. link=https://pagerduty.example/INC-2026
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026 assigned to Alex (on-call). Escalation policy: sampel-sre -> infra-leads. Priority: P1.
Alex: Acked. I'm on it, pulling graphs now. @Maya @Sam FYI will update in thread.
Alex: Running quick query on limiter metrics: `sum(rate(limiter_429_total[1m])) by (service,region)` — seeing a cluster-wide bump starting ~04:11 UTC, peaks at 14% 429s.
Maya: Noted. Any tenant skew or single-tenant blowup?
Alex: Checking tenant breakdown: `topk(10, sum(rate(limiter_429_total[5m])) by (tenant_id))` — two tenants (t-981 and t-12) show disproportionate share (40%+). But there's also a large tail of small tenants.
Sam: Support: I'm starting to see multiple customer reports for slow/gens/responses, mainly EU customers. Tagging support ticket ids: SUP-4521, SUP-4522.
Jordan: Can we confirm if quota-mapper configs were rolled out in last 30m? CI/CD shows a rollout at 03:58 UTC for quota-mapper v2.1.9 to canary, but full rollout scheduled at 04:05 and maybe failed partial.
Lina: I see a config push to quota-mapper: `deploy/infra/quota-mapper@v2.1.9` at 04:05:21Z, but the rollout logs show some nodes reported `heartbeat lost` during validation.
Alex: Hypothesis: misapplied tenant quota map -> requests get incorrectly mapped to lower quota bucket -> limiter returns 429. Alternate: limiter heartbeat/regenerator bug caused stale token windows. We need quick mitigation: stop the rollout or revert quota-mapper, and enable fallback route to legacy-mapper.
Maya: Agreed. Plan: 1) Pause deployment and rollback quota-mapper to v2.1.8. 2) Enable fallback mapping (feature flag) to legacy mapper for affected region. 3) Temporarily increase soft quota for t-981 and t-12 to reduce customer impact. 4) Keep rate limiting service in monitoring with increased sampling.
Alex: Taking step 1 now: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/quota-mapper --to-revision=rev-2.1.8` — executing.
incident-bot: Action logged: rollback started by Alex at 2026-03-14T04:20:22Z.
Alex: Rollback command issued. Watching pods restart.
Lina: I'm toggling the feature flag fallback:mapping->legacy (region=us,eu). Command: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/ff/toggle -d '{"flag":"fallback_mapping","state":"on","scope":["us","eu"]}'`
Jordan: Increasing soft quota for tenants t-981 & t-12 via admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/t-981/quota -d '{"soft_limit": "x2-temp","expire":"+30m"}'` — doing it now.
Sam: Support notified customers in SUP-4521 and SUP-4522 that we're investigating and applying mitigations. No status page update yet until we confirm impact scope.
Alex: Pods for quota-mapper back to v2.1.8. Health checks passing. Early signs: 429 rate dropping from 14% -> 6% in last 2m.
Maya: Nice. Lina, did fallback flag apply cleanly?
Lina: Yes, feature flag is on. Telemetry shows ~8% of traffic routed to legacy-mapper for US/EU.
incident-bot: Metric alert suppressed by auto-suppression (alert-id:limiter-429-anom) due to active mitigation.
Alex: Continuing to observe. Running `curl` against /v1/generate for some affected tenants to verify end-to-end. Getting successful responses now, with occasional 503s from overloaded edge but much fewer 429s.
Jordan: Heartbeat checks: limiter nodes across 3 AZs show one node in eu-west with irregular heartbeat at 04:18-04:22. That node was also part of the v2.1.9 rollout. Could be root cause.
Maya: We should cordon that node for deeper analysis. If heartbeat instability caused mapping mismatch that could explain unmapped tenants being rate limited.
Alex: Cordon and drain candidate node = limiter-eu-3. `kubectl cordon limiter-eu-3` then `kubectl drain limiter-eu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` queued.
Lina: Node cordoned and drain started. Replacements coming up.
Sam: Support: customers report improvement, SUP-4521 updated. We're drafting an initial status update for status.redwood.ai: "Degraded: rate limiting anomalies causing 5-15% 429s for a subset of tenants. Mitigations in progress." Wants approval to post.
Maya: Post the status page now with the wording above, include ETA 30m for stabilization.
Sam: Posted status update. Link=https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-update1
Alex: 429s down to ~3% overall. Request latencies also improving. Keeping monitoring for 15 more minutes.
Jordan: After drain, failed node showed mapping cache corruption on restart logs: `ERROR quota-mapper cache: key mismatch for tenant_id t-981 -> assigned bucket 0 (expected 1000)` — suggests state-sync bug.
Maya: Good find. This aligns with rollback hypothesis. Create follow-up action item to lock rollout and add additional canary validation on mapping caches.
Lina: I'll file a hotfix PR to add additional validation: verify tenant mapping checksum after startup and fail fast.
Alex: PD: I'm going to close the immediate page if metrics stay stable for another 10m. Anyone object?
Sam: Support ok with that, customers seeing recovery.
Jordan: Ops agrees. Postmortem required; tag eng-runtime and infra.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alex changed status to "acknowledged -> resolved" at 2026-03-14T04:30:50Z (INC-2026).
Alex: Marking incident as mitigated. Summary: rollback quota-mapper v2.1.9 -> v2.1.8, enable fallback mapping, increase soft quotas for two hot-tenants, drain a faulty limiter node. Impact: 5-15% 429s across prod for ~20m, concentrated on t-981 & t-12, several customer tickets. Next steps: hotfix for cache validation, improve canary checks, update runbook to include fallback flag checklist.
Maya: I'll schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:00 PT. Invite list: eng-runtime, infra, sres, support, product.
Sam: I'll follow up with customers and update SUP tickets with mitigation details and a timeline.
Lina: PR filed: infra/quota-mapper #324 — adds checksum validation and stricter rollout gating.
Alex: Thanks team. Leaving monitoring for one more cycle then moving to followups. Closing thread in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:
Sam: Adding post-incident support notes to the incident doc.
Maya: Great work.
Alex: Incident closed.
